items.title: Laboratory geometry: a restricted inertial chart, its spatial slices and fixed-time fields
items.statement:
Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be an oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space
([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]), let $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ be an inertial
frame with inertial chart $x:A\to\mathbb R^4$
([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]), let $c>0$ be the framework's
conversion constant, and let $\delta$ be the Euclidean spatial form of that
frame on $n^\perp$, $n:=e_0$, with norm $|\cdot|$ and positive spatial
orientation ([[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]). Fix a
nonempty open interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ ([[def-interval]]) and a nonempty
open set $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$, and put

$$U:=\{p\in A:\ \text{there are }t\in I,\ y\in\Omega\text{ with }x^0(p)=ct,\ (x^1,x^2,x^3)(p)=y\}.$$

Then:

(a) [Chart restriction] $x(U)=\{(ct,y):t\in I,\ y\in\Omega\}$ and
$\Phi:U\to I\times\Omega$, $\Phi(p):=(x^0(p)/c,(x^1,x^2,x^3)(p))$, is a
bijection, because the inertial chart $x:A\to\mathbb R^4$ is a bijection and
$c>0$; its components are the **laboratory time coordinate**
$t(p):=x^0(p)/c$ and the **laboratory position**
$r(p):=(x^1(p),x^2(p),x^3(p))$. In the chart coordinates the pair
$(t(p),r(p))$ is the reading of the laboratory decomposition of $p$. Writing
$r(p)=(r^1(p),r^2(p),r^3(p))\in\mathbb R^3$, the standard basis of
$\mathbb R^3$ ([[lem-standard-basis-of-f-n]]) labels the three coordinate
directions, and the identification $\mathbb R^3\cong n^\perp$ is the linear
map $\sum_{i=1}^3 r^i e_i$ into the three-dimensional real vector space
$n^\perp$ ([[def-vector-space]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]).

(b) [Slices and spatial structure] For each $t\in I$ the slice
$U_t:=\{p\in U:t(p)=t\}$ is carried bijectively onto $\Omega$ by $r$; the
constant vector $n=e_0$ is future unit timelike, and $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ is the
$\delta$-orthonormal positively oriented basis of $n^\perp$ in which the
coordinates of $r$ are expressed.

(c) [Laboratory fields] A **laboratory field of rank $m$** is a map
$F:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^m$; it is identified with the map $U\to\mathbb R^m$,
$p\mapsto F(r(p),t(p))$, and with the family $(F(\cdot,t))_{t\in I}$ of maps
$\Omega\to\mathbb R^m$, its values at fixed time. Such a field is of class
$C^k$ when the map $(y,t)\mapsto F(y,t)$ is $C^k$ in the sense of
[[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]; then $\partial_{y_i}F$ (at fixed
$t$) and $\partial_tF$ (at fixed $y$) are the partial derivatives of
[[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]. No regularity of a field is
asserted beyond the class stated for it.

(d) [Conventions] The product decomposition is a coordinate identification
inside the single inertial frame $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$; it is not a Galilean
transformation, it does not compare two inertial frames, and it does not
assert absolute simultaneity. The objects $I,\Omega,t,r,\delta$ and the
identification $\mathbb R^3\cong n^\perp$ belong to the named frame; changes
of inertial description are the proper orthochronous maps adopted in
[[post-sr-inertial-covariance]]. The frame is an origin together with an
ordered basis; it is not a congruence of observers, and no moving observer
field is defined here.
items.strategy: A construction definition with elementary verifications. The inertial chart $x$ of [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]] is a bijection, so its restriction to the set of events whose chart coordinates lie in $cI\times\Omega$ has image $cI\times\Omega$; composing with the bijection $cI\times\Omega\to I\times\Omega$, $(ct,y)\mapsto(t,y)$ (bijective because $c>0$) gives the bijection $\Phi$. Each slice $U_t$ is $\Phi^{-1}(\{t\}\times\Omega)$, on which $r$ restricts to a bijection onto $\Omega$. The claims about $n$, $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$, $\delta$ and the orientation are exactly the content of [[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]; the $C^k$ notion is that of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]] and the two kinds of partial derivative are those of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]] applied to the product coordinates. Clause (d) records conventions only: the frame dependence of $r,\delta$ and slices is stated rather than hidden, and no Galilean or observer-congruence claim is made. Nothing here uses a theorem of the framework, and the laboratory region may be a proper subset of $A$; no global chart of $A$ other than the given inertial chart is asserted.

items.title: Framework-local SI units, the vacuum constants and the exact/measured status of their values
items.statement:
Adopt the SI system of units for this framework, with the following quantity
table and conventions; every symbol is a quantity of this framework and the
laboratory structure is that of [[def-em-lab-geometry]].

(a) [Coordinates and constants] $x^0=ct$ and each spatial coordinate $x^i$
carries the metre (m); the time coordinate $t$ carries the second (s); the
conversion constant $c>0$ carries m s$^{-1}$ and has the exact SI defining
value $c=299\,792\,458\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; the elementary charge $e$ has the
exact SI defining value $e=1.602\,176\,634\times10^{-19}\ \mathrm{C}$, and this
item does not assert that physical charge is quantised; the magnetic constant
$\mu_0>0$ carries N A$^{-2}$ and is measured, so no exact numerical value of
$\mu_0$ is asserted. The pre-2019 SI fixed the historical nominal
$\mu_{0,\mathrm{nom}}:=4\pi\times10^{-7}\ \mathrm{H\,m^{-1}}
=4\pi\times10^{-7}\ \mathrm{N\,A^{-2}}$ exactly; since the revised SI took
effect on 20 May 2019, $\mu_0$ is experimentally determined. The SI brochure
quotes the nominal $\mu_{0,\mathrm{nom}}$ as the estimate at the 2019 adoption
with relative standard uncertainty $2.3\times10^{-10}$; this is historical
estimate and uncertainty context, not an exact equality for the actual $\mu_0$
or a current measured value. The electric constant is defined within the
framework by

$$\varepsilon_0:=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$$

in F m$^{-1}$, consistent with the exact SI relation $\varepsilon_0\mu_0=1/c^2$,
so that $c^2\varepsilon_0\mu_0=1$ and $\varepsilon_0$ inherits the relative
standard uncertainty of $\mu_0$.

(b) [Electromagnetic quantities] Charge $q$ carries the coulomb (C); the
charge density $\rho$ of the framework's source definition carries C m$^{-3}$
and the current density $J$ carries A m$^{-2}$, so that the four-current
components $(c\rho,J)$ carry A m$^{-2}$; the electric field $E$ carries
V m$^{-1}$; the magnetic field $B$ carries the tesla (T), where
$1\ \mathrm{T}=1\ \mathrm{N\,A^{-1}\,m^{-1}}$; the scalar potential $\varphi$
carries V and the vector potential $A$ carries T m, so that the four-potential
components $(\varphi/c,A)$ carry T m; the components of the electromagnetic
two-form of the framework's tensor definition carry T; a force carries the
newton (N), $1\ \mathrm{N}=1\ \mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-2}}$.

(c) [Mechanical quantities] A rest mass parameter $m$ carries the kilogram
(kg) and a four-momentum $P=mU$ of the relativistic particle model carries
kg m s$^{-1}$; field energy density carries J m$^{-3}$, energy flux
W m$^{-2}$, so that $1\ \mathrm{W}=1\ \mathrm{J\,s^{-1}}=1\ \mathrm{V\,A}$.

(d) [Bookkeeping only] The unit of a quantity records the adopted system of
units; it does not show that a quantity is primitive in this or any other
framework, it contains no measurement, and it does not identify a quantity
with a similarly named quantity of another framework. The exact defining
values of $c$ and $e$ fix numerical conventions of the SI; they do not by
themselves identify $c$ with the vacuum propagation constant of ideal light,
which is the physical adoption of the framework's Minkowski postulate.
items.strategy: A convention definition: it fixes the coordinate normalisation $x^0=ct$, the unit of each quantity used in this framework, the exact SI defining values of $c$ and $e$ and the measured status of $\mu_0$. The exact values $c=299\,792\,458$ m/s and $e=1.602\,176\,634\times10^{-19}$ C, and the statements that the new definition of the ampere fixes $e$ rather than $\mu_0$, that $\mu_0$ must now be determined experimentally, and that $\varepsilon_0\mu_0=1/c^2$ remains exact, are taken from the SI brochure's defining-constants table and its ampere section. The framework's definition of $\varepsilon_0$ by $(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ is a definition consistent with that exact relation; the uncertainty carried by $\varepsilon_0$ is recorded rather than hidden. The dimensional checks of the framework's equations and couplings are developed on the companion examples page of this pair. No exact or current measured numerical value of $\mu_0$ is asserted and no experiment is claimed. The historical nominal and adoption uncertainty are explicitly source context, not a substitution for the current experimentally determined constant.

items.title: Charge parameter, frame charge and current densities, volume charge and flux, and the four-current
items.statement:
Let the laboratory region and its chart be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], with the units of [[def-em-si-conventions]]. (a) [Charge parameter] The framework takes a real charge parameter $q\in\mathbb R$, measured in coulombs, attached to a source; its sign is the sign of the source and it is a parameter of the model. Charge quantisation is not asserted. (b) [Smooth source fields] A smooth (volume) source field on $\Omega\times I$ is a pair $(\rho,J)$ of maps $\rho:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R$, $J:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ that is continuous on $\Omega\times I$ and of class $C^1$ wherever a displayed equation differentiates it; $\rho$ is the frame charge density (C m$^{-3}$) and $J$ the frame current density (A m$^{-2}$). For each fixed $t\in I$ retain the compact Jordan branch: if $V\subseteq\Omega$ is compact and Jordan measurable, define $Q_R(V,t):=\int_V\rho(y,t)dy$ by [[def-riemann-integral-over-a-jordan-set]], with integrability supplied by [[thm-continuous-functions-on-compact-jordan-sets-are-integrable]]. For the full measurable-volume branch assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), as required by the published Lebesgue-measure interface. If $V$ is any bounded Lebesgue-measurable subset with compact closure $\overline V\subseteq\Omega$, define
$$Q(V,t):=\int_V\rho(y,t)d\lambda_3(y)=\int_{\mathbb R^3}F_t(y)\mathbf1_V(y)d\lambda_3(y),$$
where $F_t=\rho(\cdot,t)$ on $\Omega$ and $0$ elsewhere; the signed integral is defined through its positive and negative parts ([[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]], [[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]]). This integral is absolutely finite, since $\rho(\cdot,t)$ is bounded on $\overline V$ and $V$ has finite Lebesgue measure. On the compact Jordan branch, under the same Countable Choice assumption, $Q=Q_R$ by [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]]. The empty region has charge zero in both branches. The current flux remains defined independently: for each oriented surface patch in $\Omega$ with unit normal field $n_S$ the current flux at time $t$ is $\int_S J(y,t)\cdot n_S(y)\,dS$ ([[def-oriented-unit-normal-and-flux-of-a-surface-patch]]). Point sources and sheet sources are not source fields in this sense; they are different objects, defined by their own pairings when the framework uses them. (c) [Covariant identification] Write $j:=(c\rho,J)$, so $j^0=c\rho$ and $j^i=J^i$. The framework adopts as a model premise the identification of the charge-current of a source with a vector field of the affine Minkowski model, and hence the component transformation law of [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] for $j$ between inertial charts. This is a model premise, not a theorem about physical currents. (d) [Frame density, scalar multiplier and the normalized material branch] Suppose additionally that the identified $j$ is $C^1$ and $j=\rho_0U$, with a $C^1$ future timelike vector field $U$ and a $C^1$ real scalar multiplier $\rho_0$. Since $U^0>0$, define the normalized chart direction $u:=U/U^0$, so $u^0=1$, $u^i=U^i/U^0$. Then $j=(\rho_0U^0)u$ and, because the electromagnetic convention is $j^0=c\rho$,
$$\rho=\rho_0U^0/c,\qquad J^i=\rho_0U^i=c\rho\,u^i.$$
Pointwise equality $\rho=\rho_0$ holds if and only if $\rho_0(U^0-c)=0$, including the zero-multiplier case. Where $\rho_0\ne0$, equality is equivalent to $U^0=c$, which does not alone imply $U^i=0$ for an arbitrary future timelike $U$. Thus a scalar multiplier is not automatically a Lorentz rest charge density. The direction $u$ is chart normalized, with no unit or proper-four-velocity normalization imposed in this general branch; if its coordinate velocity interpretation is adopted, the spatial velocity is $v^i:=cu^i$.
For the separate convective source model, explicitly assume that $U$ is the material proper-time four-velocity, normalized by $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$ as in [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]. This is an additional model condition, not a consequence of the factorization $j=\rho_0U$. In that branch, $U=\gamma(c,v)$, $|v|<c$, $\gamma=(1-|v|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$, and
$$\rho=\gamma\rho_0,\qquad J=\rho v.$$
Here $\rho_0$ is the rest charge density of this stipulated convective model: in a comoving inertial frame $U=(c,0,0,0)$ and $j=(c\rho_0,0,0,0)$. The equality $\rho=\rho_0$ then holds exactly where $\rho_0=0$ or $v=0$ (equivalently $\gamma=1$). Both signs of charge and the zero-density case are retained. (e) [Scope] This definition fixes the source objects of the smooth branch and their transformation interface. It asserts no conservation law (that is proved for stated source classes) and no regularity of singular sources.
items.strategy:
Keep clauses (a)-(c) as explicit source types and the adopted physical identification. The compact Jordan branch uses [[thm-continuous-functions-on-compact-jordan-sets-are-integrable]] and [[def-riemann-integral-over-a-jordan-set]]; flux uses [[def-oriented-unit-normal-and-flux-of-a-surface-patch]]. For the broader Lebesgue branch assume the explicitly stated Countable Choice, without Dependent Choice or a convergence/FTC assumption. Fix $t$ and an admitted nonempty $V$. The continuous function $\rho(\cdot,t)$ is bounded by $M_t<\infty$ in absolute value on compact $\overline V$ by [[thm-extreme-value-metric]]. Its zero extension $F_t$ is Borel: for every open $O\subseteq\mathbb R$, the inverse image inside the open set $\Omega$ is relatively open and hence open in $\mathbb R^3$; add the closed complement of $\Omega$ precisely when $0\in O$. This is also the open-set form of [[thm-continuous-preimages-of-borel-sets-are-borel]]. Under Countable Choice, Borel sets are Lebesgue measurable ([[thm-borel-sets-are-lebesgue-measurable]]) and bounded measurable $V$ has finite measure ([[prop-lebesgue-measure-is-sigma-finite-and-finite-on-bounded-sets]]). Positive/negative parts and their restrictions by $\mathbf1_V$ are measurable by [[prop-closure-properties-of-measurable-functions-used-by-the-integral]]. The bound $|F_t|\mathbf1_V\le M_t\mathbf1_V$ and [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]] give
$$\int|F_t|\mathbf1_Vd\lambda_3\le M_t\lambda_3(V)<\infty,$$
where the indicator integral is its simple-function value by [[prop-the-nonnegative-integral-agrees-with-the-simple-integral]]. This proves exactly the absolute signed integrability required by [[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]] and defines $Q$ using the nonnegative restrictions of [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]]. For empty $V$ the product is zero. On compact Jordan $V$, the continuous density restricted to V has a bounded Borel zero extension to a bounding rectangle, so the exact compact-Jordan clause of [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]], also under Countable Choice, identifies the two finite integral values. The algebraic supplier [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]](vii) gives $j=\rho_0U=\rho_0U^0u$; its coordinate density is $j^0$, whereas the present SI source convention defines $j^0=c\rho$. Division by $c>0$ gives $\rho=\rho_0U^0/c$ and $\rho-\rho_0=\rho_0(U^0-c)/c$, proving exactly the stated equality cases. The spatial components give $J^i=c\rho u^i$. Neither $U^0=c$ nor chart normalization $u^0=1$ is a proper-four-velocity condition.
In the additional normalized material model, write $v=c(U^1,U^2,U^3)/U^0$. The norm equation $-(U^0)^2+|U_{\mathrm{sp}}|^2=-c^2$ gives $(U^0)^2(1-|v|^2/c^2)=c^2$, and future timelikeness gives $U^0>0$ and $|v|<c$, so $U^0=c\gamma$. This is the exact four-velocity/relative-velocity content of [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]; substitution gives $\rho=\gamma\rho_0$ and $J=\rho v$. In its comoving frame $U^0=c$, hence the source convention identifies the scalar multiplier with the stipulated rest-frame density. Since $\gamma=1$ if and only if $v=0$, the normalized equality cases follow, including $\rho_0=0$. All density readings remain within the adopted current model; no conservation, measurement, general current factorization, force law or singular-source regularity is deduced.

items.title: The electric and magnetic fields as fixed-time spatial vector fields
items.statement:
Let the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$, its spatial Euclidean structure
and its units be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] and
[[def-em-si-conventions]], and let $k\ge1$. An **electric field of class
$C^k$** on the region is a map $E:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ that is of class
$C^k$ in the sense of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]; a
**magnetic field of class $C^k$** is a map $B:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ of
the same class. At fixed $t\in I$ the maps $E(\cdot,t),B(\cdot,t):\Omega\to
\mathbb R^3$ are real spatial vector fields on the region $\Omega$, read in the
$\delta$-orthonormal basis $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of the frame. The framework uses:
$C^1$ fields in the classical Maxwell branch, $C^2$ fields where second or
mixed time-space derivatives of the fields appear, and $C^\infty$ fields in
the smooth existence branches; every statement carries its own regularity and
no regularity beyond it is asserted.

Conventions:

(a) The **polar-vector** and **axial-vector** conventions mean the following
component rules under a spatial orthogonal coordinate change $y'=Qy$, where
$Q$ is a real $3\times3$ matrix with $Q^{\mathsf T}Q=I_3$. Transpose,
matrix product and identity are those of [[def-transpose-of-a-matrix]] and
[[def-matrix-product-and-identity-matrix]], and $\det Q$ is the determinant
of [[def-determinant-of-a-square-matrix]]. At corresponding
points $E'(y',t)=QE(y,t)$ and $B'(y',t)=(\det Q)QB(y,t)$. Thus polar and axial
components agree in their transformation rule when $\det Q=1$ and differ by
a sign when $\det Q=-1$. These rules specify the orientation convention;
the adopted inertial descriptions have positive orientation, and no physical
orientation-reversing change of description is adopted here.

(b) The fields are defined by their values on $\Omega\times I$, and no value at
a point of singular source support is asserted.

(c) $E$ carries V m$^{-1}$ and $B$ carries T.

(d) The identification of the pair $(E,B)$ with the components of an
alternating two-form, including its transformation behaviour, is made in the
framework's electromagnetic two-form definition on this page and is not
presupposed here.
items.strategy: An explicit type/domain/convention definition: the fields are maps on the product $\Omega\times I$ of the laboratory region with a stated class of regularity, and their fixed-time readings are spatial vector fields in the frame basis. The regularity notion is that of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]; the polar/axial convention and the exclusion of pointwise values at singular source support are conventions recorded explicitly rather than used implicitly. No differential equation and no derived quantity is introduced by this definition.

items.title: Adopted Minkowski physical model of the electromagnetic framework
items.statement:
Adopt as physical assumptions of this framework:

(i) The oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ used by
[[def-em-lab-geometry]], together with the
conversion constant $c>0$ of [[def-em-si-conventions]], is the spacetime of the
framework: its points represent idealized physical events, displacements
represent idealized spacetime separations, and the causal classification of the
model is the framework's causal structure. In the concrete coordinate
realization [[def-em-minkowski-affine-space]], $A=V=\mathbb R^4$ and
$\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. That supplier uses the symbol $C^+$ for
the nonzero future causal cone, including null vectors; here, as in the
special-relativity model, $C^+$ denotes its future timelike subset. The
future null boundary vectors retain their separate causal classification.

(ii) The inertial frames and charts of
[[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]] are the inertial descriptions of the
framework, and changes of description are the proper orthochronous isometries
adopted in [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]].

(iii) The ideal clock reading rule along future timelike curves and the
identification of ideal vacuum light rays with future null straight lines, both
with the same constant $c$, are those adopted in
[[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]].

(iv) The laboratory description of fields and sources is the restricted
inertial chart of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], with the spatial Euclidean structure
and the SI conventions of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] and
[[def-em-si-conventions]].

Status and scope: the mathematical model defines the geometry and its theorems
prove geometric facts only; that physical events are described by the model,
that ideal clocks read the stated proper time and that ideal vacuum light
follows null straight lines are adopted assumptions, not deductions from
experiment or from the mathematical axioms. The special-relativity postulates
adopted here do not by themselves select the Maxwell equations, a force law or
any matter model: the electromagnetic equations and couplings of this framework
are further postulates of it. The framework is classical, flat and non-quantum;
gravitational curvature, quantum fields and measurement postulates are outside
its scope.
items.strategy: A postulate, not a theorem: it records the adopted physical reading of the mathematical Minkowski model of [[def-em-minkowski-affine-space]] and reuses the two special-relativity physical postulates [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]] and [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]] with the shared constant $c$ as the vacuum propagation constant. The exposition must separate what the mathematical model fixes (the affine geometry, its causal cones, its frames) from what is adopted (the event interpretation, the clock and light interpretation, the inertial-description equivalence). It must also state that Maxwell's equations and the Lorentz coupling are additional postulates not implied by the SR assumptions, and it asserts no empirical measurement or verification.

items.title: Worldlines, four-velocity, chart readings and the frame/observer distinction
items.statement:
The particle and light objects of the framework are the following curves and
vector fields of the affine Minkowski model ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]],
[[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]), with the physical interpretation of
[[post-em-minkowski-physical-model]] and the units of
[[def-em-si-conventions]].

(a) [Worldlines] A **worldline** is a regular causal curve $x:J\to A$ in one of
the regularity classes of [[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]] ($J$ an
order-convex subset of $\mathbb R$ with at least two elements). A **massive
worldline** is a $C^k$ future timelike worldline, $k\ge1$, with everywhere
nonzero future timelike tangent. A **future null curve** is a $C^1$ curve with
everywhere nonzero future null tangent. An **ideal vacuum light ray** of the
adopted physical model follows a null straight line: on its parameter interval
it has the form $x(s)=p+\lambda(s)v$, where $p\in A$, $v\in V$ is nonzero
future null, and $\lambda$ is $C^1$ with $\lambda'(s)>0$. This is the
straight-ray adoption of [[post-em-minkowski-physical-model]]; arbitrary
future null curves are retained as kinematic objects without asserting that
they describe vacuum light propagation. Along a null curve the integrand
$-\eta(x',x')$ of the proper-time construction
([[def-sr-proper-time]]) vanishes identically, so that construction yields no
proper-time parametrization of it, and a light ray is never treated as a
massive worldline. A worldline is a curve in spacetime; its reading $r\circ x$
in a named laboratory chart is a coordinate description of it, not an object of
another observer.

(b) [Four-velocity and four-acceleration] For a massive worldline the
four-velocity $U$ and, when it is $C^2$, the four-acceleration $A$ are those of
[[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]]; wherever defined they satisfy
$\eta(U,U)=-c^2$ and $\eta(U,A)=0$, by
[[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]].

(c) [Chart reading] If a massive $C^2$ worldline is described in a laboratory
chart of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] by $t\mapsto(ct,r(t))$ on an open interval of
laboratory times, then $|r'(t)|<c$ for every $t$, with four-velocity
$U=\gamma(c,r')$ and Lorentz factor
$\gamma=(1-|r'|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$, by clause (e) of
[[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]].

(d) [Frames and observers] An inertial frame in this framework is the
origin-with-basis object of [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]; a point
observer is a future unit timelike vector $n\in V$ with rest space $n^\perp$ and
rest projection $h$, as in clauses (c)-(d) of
[[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]. On an open spacetime region
$W\subseteq A$, an **observer congruence field** means a $C^1$ map $n:W\to V$ with
$n(p)$ future timelike and $\eta(n(p),n(p))=-1$ at every $p$; its observer
histories, when given, are integral curves satisfying $dx/d\tau=cn(x)$.
A **tetrad field** is a tuple of $C^1$ maps $(f_0,f_1,f_2,f_3):W\to V^4$
whose values form a positively oriented $\eta$-orthonormal basis at every
event, with $f_0$ future timelike. Regularity here means componentwise $C^1$
in inertial coordinates. These fields need not be constant and are distinct
from an inertial origin-with-basis frame, its coordinate chart and a single
point observer; no global congruence or tetrad is asserted to exist.

(e) [Scope] No force law, no self-field and no extended-body structure is
supplied here; an accelerating massive worldline requires a force model stated
separately, and an ideal light ray carries no dispersive, quantum or
polarisation structure in this definition.
items.strategy: Definition-only formulation: regular causal curves with SR endpoint conventions, future timelike massive curves, straight regular future-null ideal rays, proper-time derivatives, and explicitly typed C1 observer and tetrad fields. No field existence or proof of a physical assumption is asserted.

items.title: The microscopic vacuum Maxwell equations: smooth and weak branches
items.statement:
Adopt as a physical postulate of this framework the following four equations for the fields of [[def-em-fields]] and the sources of [[def-em-sources]] on the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$ of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], with $\mu_0>0$, $c>0$, $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ and the SI units of [[def-em-si-conventions]]. (a) [Smooth branch] Let $E,B$ be jointly $C^1$ fields with the additional derivatives required by each equation existing and continuous, and let $\rho,J$ be continuous. Then, with the divergence and curl of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] and the partial derivative $\partial_t$ at fixed position of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]],

$$\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad \operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB,\qquad \operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE.$$

(b) [Weak branch] Let instead $E,B$ be locally integrable $\mathbb R^3$-valued fields and $\rho,J$ locally integrable scalar and vector fields on $I\times\Omega$, identified with their regular distributions ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]). Let $\operatorname{div}$, $\operatorname{curl}$ and $\partial_t$ act as distributional derivatives, and let $\psi$ range over $C_c^\infty(I\times\Omega)$ ([[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]]). Then the same four identities hold in the sense of [[def-distribution]]: the pairings $\langle\operatorname{div}E-\rho/\varepsilon_0,\psi\rangle$, $\langle\operatorname{div}B,\psi\rangle$, $\langle\operatorname{curl}E+\partial_tB,\psi\rangle$ and $\langle\operatorname{curl}B-\mu_0J-c^{-2}\partial_tE,\psi\rangle$ vanish for every such $\psi$, all derivatives being distributional derivatives ([[def-distributional-derivative]]). (c) [Scope] The postulate contains no magnetic charge: $\operatorname{div}B=0$ and no magnetic-source term appears in $\operatorname{curl}E$. Sources that are not locally integrable functions (point or sheet sources) are covered by neither branch and require their own definition. The equations are adopted classical vacuum physics in the named inertial chart; they are not deduced from charge conservation, from empirical agreement or from the special-relativity postulates, and this item by itself asserts no covariance under changes of inertial frame.
items.strategy: A postulate, not a theorem. Obligations and conventions: the fields and sources are those of [[def-em-fields]] and [[def-em-sources]], the operators are the published divergence and curl of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] and the partial derivative of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]], and the weak reading uses exactly the regular-distribution embedding, the test space and the distributional derivative named in the statement. The exposition must state that the four equations are adopted, that the choice of the sign and constant conventions is the one fixed by [[def-em-si-conventions]], and that no magnetic charge is included; the sources not covered by either branch are excluded explicitly. Empirical support for Maxwell's equations is a nonlogical relation of the framework, not a proof, and no verification is claimed here.

items.title: The electromagnetic two-form, its observer decomposition and the four-current
items.statement:
Let the laboratory region, its inertial chart and the fields and sources be those
of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], [[def-em-fields]] and [[def-em-sources]], with the
units of [[def-em-si-conventions]]; fix the ordered basis
$(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of the chart and the oriented volume form $\varepsilon$ of
[[def-oriented-minkowski-volume-form]], with $\varepsilon_{0123}=+1$ and
$\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$.

(a) [Components] For a field pair $(E,B)$ of class $C^k$, $k\ge1$, define the
covariant components of the **electromagnetic two-form** $F$ in the chart by
$F_{00}=0$, $F_{0i}:=-E_i/c$, $F_{ij}:=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$
($i,j,k\in\{1,2,3\}$) and $F_{ab}:=-F_{ba}$, the index-raised components being
$F^{0i}=E_i/c$, $F^{i0}=-E_i/c$ and $F^{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$. Here
$\epsilon_{ijk}$ is the spatial permutation symbol of
[[def-oriented-minkowski-volume-form]]. Then $F$ is a $C^k$ type-$(0,2)$
tensor field on $U$ in the sense of
[[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]], alternating at every event, and the
components above are exactly its component functions: at $p\in U$ the tensor
$F(p)$ is the bilinear form $F(p)(u,w)=F_{ab}(p)u^aw^b$ on $V$ in the
coordinates $u^a,w^b$ of $u,w$ in $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$. Indeed each $F_{ab}$ is
a finite sum of products of the $C^k$ functions $E_i,B_k$ of the chart
coordinates with the constants $c,\epsilon_{ijk}$, hence a $C^k$ function of
$x(p)$, and the component criterion of
[[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]] applies.

(b) [Observer decomposition] Let $n:=e_0$ be the future unit timelike vector of
the chart and let $e_a:=F_{ab}n^b$, $b_a:=(*F)_{ab}n^b$ be the observer
components of [[thm-sr-antisymmetric-observer-decomposition]]; then
$e_i=+E_i/c$, $b_i=-B_i$ and $e_0=b_0=0$, and the invariants and square wedge
of that theorem read

$$\tfrac12F_{ab}F^{ab}=|B|^2-|E|^2/c^2,\qquad F_{ab}(*F)^{ab}=+4\,(E\cdot B)/c,\qquad F\wedge F=-2\,(E\cdot B)\,\varepsilon/c,$$

where $|\cdot|$ and $\cdot$ are the spatial Euclidean structure of the frame.
(For the same pair $(E,B)$, that theorem's optional clause (d) uses
$F_{\rm optional}^{i0}=E_i/c$ and $F_{\rm optional}^{ij}=-\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$, so
$F_{\rm optional}=-F$ in all six components, not only the magnetic block. This
framework fixes clause (a) and uses the theorem's general algebra; its optional
SI dictionary must be converted by negating the entire tensor.)

(c) [Potentials when they exist] If $\varphi$ and $A$ are $C^1$ with
$E=-\nabla\varphi-\partial_tA$ and $B=\operatorname{curl}A$, and
$A^\mu:=(\varphi/c,A)$, $A_\mu:=\eta_{\mu\nu}A^\nu$, then
$F_{\mu\nu}=\partial_\mu A_\nu-\partial_\nu A_\mu$; conversely, if a $C^1$
covector field $A_\mu$ on $U$ satisfies $F_{\mu\nu}=\partial_\mu A_\nu
-\partial_\nu A_\mu$, then $E,B$ recovered from $F$ by clause (a) obey
$E=-\nabla\varphi-\partial_tA$ and $B=\operatorname{curl}A$ with
$\varphi:=-cA_0$ and the spatial potential vector $A:=(A_1,A_2,A_3)$. Here
$\nabla$ and $\operatorname{curl}$ are those of
[[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] in the spatial coordinates,
and the spatial cross-product conventions of [[def-cross-product-in-r3]] are
used. The definition does not assert that every field pair admits such a
potential; where a $C^1$ potential represents the $C^1$-or-better field of
clause (a), the field is closed in the explicit sense
$\partial_\lambda F_{\mu\nu}+\partial_\mu F_{\nu\lambda}
+\partial_\nu F_{\lambda\mu}=0$. This conclusion does not require second
classical derivatives of the potential: put
$H_{\lambda\mu\nu}:=\partial_\lambda F_{\mu\nu}+\partial_\mu F_{\nu\lambda}
+\partial_\nu F_{\lambda\mu}$, which is continuous because $F$ is $C^1$; for
every smooth compactly supported test $\psi$, substituting $F=dA$ and
integrating by parts twice, moving the derivatives first onto $\psi$
([[lem-sr-compact-variation-and-fundamental-lemma]] (b)) and then off the
potential factors after commuting only the smooth test derivatives
([[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]]), gives $\int H\psi=0$; the
fundamental lemma (a) of [[lem-sr-compact-variation-and-fundamental-lemma]]
then gives $H=0$. The framework's potential theorems establish existence only
under their stated hypotheses; [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]
supplies the coordinate derivatives $\partial_\mu$ used throughout.

(d) [Four-current and index-raising operator] With the adopted four-current
$j=(c\rho,J)$ of [[def-em-sources]], the raised-index operator $\Phi$ of
[[lem-em-antisymmetric-tensor-contraction]], defined pointwise on $V$ by
$\eta(\Phi(u),w)=F(w,u)$, satisfies
$\Phi(u)^\mu=\eta^{\mu\alpha}F_{\alpha\beta}u^\beta$; the components of $F$
carry the tesla (T), those of $j$ carry A m$^{-2}$, and those of a
four-potential $A^\mu$ carry T m.
items.strategy:
An explicit definition computed from the components. The components $F_{ab}$ of clause (a) are $C^k$ functions of the inertial coordinates, because they are built from the $C^k$ functions $E_i,B_k$ and the constants $c,\epsilon_{ijk}$; hence $F$ is a $C^k$ tensor field by the component criterion of [[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]], and it is alternating because $F_{ab}=-F_{ba}$ by construction. Clause (b) is a direct substitution into clauses (a)-(c) of [[thm-sr-antisymmetric-observer-decomposition]] with $n=e_0$: $e_i=F_{i0}=+E_i/c$, $b_i=-	frac12\epsilon_{ijk}F_{jk}=-B_i$, the invariants $	frac12F_{ab}F^{ab}=|b|^2-|e|^2$ and $F_{ab}(*F)^{ab}=-4\,e\cdot b$ are evaluated with these values, and the square wedge uses the theorem's normalisation $F\wedge F=2\,(e\cdot b)\,\varepsilon$. For the same E,B, the optional tensor in the supplier is the negative of the entire adopted tensor; no magnetic-only sign conversion is used. u}=\partial_\lambda F_{\mu

items.title: Superposition for prescribed Maxwell fields and sources
items.statement: Assume the vacuum Maxwell postulate [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] on the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$ of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the fields of [[def-em-fields]] and the sources of [[def-em-sources]], and fix the constants $\mu_0>0$, $c>0$, $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ of [[def-em-si-conventions]]. Let $n\ge1$, let $(E_1,B_1,\rho_1,J_1),\dots,(E_n,B_n,\rho_n,J_n)$ be $n$ field-source pairs each satisfying one and the same branch of the postulate on the same region (all in the smooth branch, or all in the weak branch), and let $a_1,\dots,a_n\in\mathbb R$. Put $E:=\sum_{j=1}^na_jE_j$, $B:=\sum_{j=1}^na_jB_j$, $\rho:=\sum_{j=1}^na_j\rho_j$ and $J:=\sum_{j=1}^na_jJ_j$. Then: (a) $(E,B,\rho,J)$ satisfies the same branch of the postulate on the same region with the same constants: pointwise in the smooth branch and in the sense of the pairings of clause (b) of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] in the weak branch. (b) Nothing beyond this linearity is asserted: the result does not apply to a source whose density depends nonlinearly on the fields (a nonlinear constitutive law), and no convergence statement is made for infinite series or integrals of solutions or for infinite linear combinations. (c) The theorem is conditional on the adopted postulate and is not an empirical claim about nature.
items.strategy: **Proof technique:** direct termwise computation, smooth branch and distributional branch separately. In the smooth branch, the divergence and curl are linear in their arguments because they are finite sums of first partial derivatives ([[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]), and $\partial_t$ is linear likewise; hence $\operatorname{div}E=\sum_ja_j\operatorname{div}E_j=\sum_ja_j\rho_j/\varepsilon_0=\rho/\varepsilon_0$ and, in the same way, $\operatorname{div}B=0$, $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$ and $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$. In the weak branch the distributional derivatives are linear and the pairings are linear in the distributions ([[def-distribution]], [[def-distributional-derivative]]), so the four vanishing pairings of the postulate for the sum follow by summing the finitely many vanishing pairings of the summands with the same test function. The scope clauses (nonlinear sources, no infinite superposition) are recorded in the theorem itself; no physical premise beyond the postulate is used, and no empirical premise occurs, so no empirical qualifications are inherited beyond the postulate's own.

items.title: The Lorentz coupling: external force on a test charge and the continuum force and power densities
items.statement:
Adopt as physical postulates of this framework, on the spacetime and particle
model of [[post-em-minkowski-physical-model]] and
[[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]] and on the special-relativity particle
model [[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]]:

(i) [Test charge in a prescribed external field] Let $q\in\mathbb R$ be a
constant charge parameter ([[def-em-sources]]), $m>0$ an externally supplied
rest mass, $x:J\to A$ a future timelike $C^2$ massive worldline with
four-velocity $U$, and let $F$ be a prescribed field of
[[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] that is $C^1$ on a neighbourhood of the graph
of $x$ and is generated externally to the particle. Adopt the equation of
motion

$$m\,\frac{dU}{d\tau}=q\,\Phi(U),$$

where, at each original parameter $s\in J$, $\Phi=\Phi_{x(s)}$ is the
raised-index operator of the field at $x(s)$, defined by
$\eta(\Phi_{x(s)}(u),w)=F(x(s))(w,u)$
([[lem-em-antisymmetric-tensor-contraction]]); equivalently
$m\,dU^\mu/d\tau=q\,F^{\mu\nu}U_\nu$. Here $dU/d\tau$ is the derivative of $U$
with respect to its proper-time function $\tau(s)$: explicitly
$dU/d\tau=U'(s)/\tau'(s)$, with
$\tau'(s)=c^{-1}\sqrt{-\eta(x'(s),x'(s))}>0$. It is the four-acceleration of the worldline
([[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]],
[[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]). The particle's own field
is excluded from $F$: this is the external-field coupling, and it defines no
self-force.

(ii) [Continuum matter coupling] For a smooth source $(\rho,J)$ of
[[def-em-sources]] interacting with the field through an explicitly stated
matter model to which this coupling applies, adopt the force density
$\rho E+J\times B$ (unit N m$^{-3}$) and the power density $J\cdot E$ (unit
W m$^{-3}$) as the electromagnetic source terms of that matter model, with the
spatial cross product of [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]; they describe the local
interaction of the field with matter and are not a property of a prescribed
current alone.

(iii) [Scope] The rest mass and the charge are inputs; $m$ is not derived within
electromagnetism. The coupling is adopted for constant $q$ and $m>0$; no
magnetic-monopole coupling, no radiation reaction and no self-force are
included. In particular the nonrelativistic coordinate statement
$mr''=q(E+r'\times B)$ is not adopted as exact: the adopted statement is the
covariant one of clause (i), and any low-speed statement requires its own
approximation hypotheses and error bounds.
items.strategy: A postulate, not a theorem. The exposition must state the exact data (constant charge, externally supplied positive rest mass, future timelike C^2 worldline, prescribed external field C^1 near the graph), name the raised-index operator $\Phi$ with its defining identity and index form from [[lem-em-antisymmetric-tensor-contraction]] so that the equation is unambiguous, and state the exclusion of the particle's own field. Clause (ii) is a formulation premise for matter models, with its units fixed by [[def-em-si-conventions]] and its cross product the spatial one of [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]; it is not a derivation from the field equations. Clause (iii) records the scope: no self-force, no radiation reaction, no magnetic monopole, and no exact Newtonian law. Empirical support for the coupling is a nonlogical relation of the framework; the item claims no verification and no measured value.

items.title: Smooth and point-source constructions: distinct for nonzero charge, both zero at zero charge
items.statement:
This example is conditional on the definitions [[def-em-sources]],
[[def-em-fields]] and the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]], and
assumes Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ both for the Lebesgue-volume
source branch and for the injectivity of the regular-distribution embedding
used below ([[def-countable-choice]]).

(a) [Smooth source] Let $f\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$ be nonnegative with
Lebesgue normalization $\int_{\mathbb R^3}f\,d\lambda_3=1$ (the Riemann
integral over any compact box containing $\operatorname{supp}f$ has the same
value by [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]])
(for instance any nonzero nonnegative smooth compactly supported bump divided
by its finite nonzero integral), let $q\in\mathbb R$, and let
$\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be a nonempty open set containing
$\operatorname{supp}f$. Then $\rho:=qf$ and $J:=0$ is a smooth source field of
[[def-em-sources]]: $\rho$ is compactly supported and of class $C^\infty$,
hence continuous, and for every bounded Lebesgue-measurable $V$ with compact
closure inside $\Omega$ and containing $\operatorname{supp}f$, the charge is
$Q(V,t)=q\int f=q$; the same value holds for the retained compact
Jordan/Riemann branch at every time $t$, so the smooth branch of
[[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] applies to this source.

(b) [Point source] Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open interval and
$z:I\to\mathbb R^3$ a $C^1$ trajectory whose graph map
$t\mapsto(z(t),t)$ is proper into $\Omega\times I$
([[lem-em-point-current-continuity]]; properness is automatic when
$\Omega\times I$ is the whole ambient domain or when $I=\mathbb R$). For
the same charge $q$ as in (a), the pairings
$\langle\rho,\psi\rangle:=q\int_I\psi(z(t),t)\,dt$ and
$\langle J,\psi\rangle:=q\int_Iz'(t)\psi(z(t),t)\,dt$, for
$\psi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega\times I)$, are the point-source distributions of
[[lem-em-point-current-continuity]]: they are distributions
([[def-distribution]], [[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]])
satisfying $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$ in the distributional sense.
At each fixed time $t$ this model assigns the charge
$q\cdot\mathbf 1_{z(t)\in V}$ to a Jordan-measurable $V\subseteq\Omega$, and its
instantaneous spatial density is the evaluation functional $q\delta_{z(t)}$
([[def-dirac-delta-and-its-derivatives]]),
$\varphi\mapsto q\,\varphi(z(t))$; a source field of the smooth branch instead
gives the integrals $\varphi\mapsto\int_\Omega\rho(y,t)\varphi(y)\,dy$ of its
continuous density.

(c) [The two classes differ] Fix $t\in I$, put $z_0:=z(t)\in\Omega$ and
suppose $q\ne0$. Retain Countable Choice for the regular-distribution
embedding and the Lebesgue-null singleton result cited below
([[def-countable-choice]]). Then no locally integrable
$\rho\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$ represents the point charge: there is no
such $\rho$ whose regular distribution
([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]]) satisfies
$\langle\rho,\varphi\rangle=q\,\varphi(z_0)$ for every
$\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$. Indeed, if $\rho$ did, then on the open set
$\Omega\setminus\{z_0\}$ every test vanishes at $z_0$, so the regular
distribution of the restriction of $\rho$ is zero, and injectivity gives
$\rho=0$ almost everywhere there
([[def-measure-null-set-and-almost-everywhere]]); since $\{z_0\}$ is
Lebesgue-null ([[prop-countable-subsets-of-rn-are-lebesgue-null]]) and a union
of two null sets is null
([[thm-finite-and-countable-subadditivity-of-measures]]), $\rho=0$ almost
everywhere on $\Omega$. The regular distribution depends only on the
almost-everywhere class, so $\langle\rho,\varphi_0\rangle=0$ for a cutoff
$\varphi_0\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ with $\varphi_0=1$ near $z_0$
([[lem-test-function-cutoffs-and-euclidean-localization]]), while the assumed
identity gives $\langle\rho,\varphi_0\rangle=q\varphi_0(z_0)=q\ne0$: a
contradiction. Hence the point source is not a source field of the smooth
branch of [[def-em-sources]] (whose densities are continuous functions), and
the smooth-branch equations are not applied to it pointwise; the point source
enters the framework only through its distributional pairings.

(d) [Conclusion] The two source classes carry the same parameter $q$ and the
same total charge $q$ (the smooth density integrates to $q$; the point model
assigns charge $q$ to regions containing the particle). For $q\ne0$ their
spatial distributions are distinct and the point source has no locally
integrable representative. For $q=0$ both constructions give the zero charge
and zero current distributions, represented by the smooth zero functions.
The nonzero point source is used only through its pairings; neither branch of
[[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] supplies a singular-source Maxwell adoption.
This example asserts no field value at $z(t)$ and
contains no measurement or empirical claim.
items.strategy: For the smooth-source charge claim in (a), assume the declared Countable Choice. The continuous density $qf$ satisfies both source-volume branches of [[def-em-sources]]. For any admitted bounded Lebesgue-measurable $V$ containing $\operatorname{supp}f$, $f\mathbf1_V=f$ pointwise. Since $f\ge0$ and $\int f=1$, it is integrable, and [[thm-linearity-of-the-lebesgue-integral-on-l-one]] gives $Q(V,t)=\int_Vqf=q\int f=q$ through [[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]] and the positive/negative restrictions of [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]]. For compact Jordan $V$, [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]] identifies this value with the Riemann charge. No new convergence or differentiation result is needed. Direct computations and one short contradiction. (a) $\rho=qf$ is $C^\infty$ with compact support, hence continuous and bounded; for a compact Jordan-measurable $V$ containing the support, the integral of $\rho$ over $V$ equals $q\int f=q$ by the definition of $f$ and additivity of the integral over the support complement ([[def-riemann-integral-over-a-jordan-set]]). (b) The pairings and the continuity equation are exactly the content of [[lem-em-point-current-continuity]] under its properness hypothesis; the fixed-time reading $q\delta_{z(t)}$ is the evaluation functional of [[def-dirac-delta-and-its-derivatives]]. (c) Suppose $u_\rho=q\delta_{z_0}$ with $\rho\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$. On the open set $\Omega\setminus\{z_0\}$, for every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega\setminus\{z_0\})$ one has $u_\rho(\varphi)=q\varphi(z_0)=0$; the injectivity clause of [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]], which carries AC_omega, gives $\rho=0$ almost everywhere on $\Omega\setminus\{z_0\}$. The singleton $\{z_0\}$ is null by [[prop-countable-subsets-of-rn-are-lebesgue-null]], and the union of the exceptional null set with $\{z_0\}$ is null by finite subadditivity ([[thm-finite-and-countable-subadditivity-of-measures]], [[def-measure-null-set-and-almost-everywhere]]), so $\rho=0$ almost everywhere on $\Omega$. By the definition of the regular distribution (which depends only on the almost-everywhere class) $u_\rho=0$, i.e. $u_\rho(\varphi)=0$ for every test. The cutoff lemma supplies $\varphi_0$ with $\varphi_0=1$ near $z_0$, and the assumed identity gives $u_\rho(\varphi_0)=q\varphi_0(z_0)=q\ne0$, a contradiction. (d) is the bookkeeping of the two total charges. No field equation is solved, no regularity of the point source is asserted beyond its distributional definition, and the only choice principle used is Countable Choice, carried explicitly both by the Lebesgue-volume/comparison branch and by the embedding theorem's injectivity. Reader correction retained and independently reviewed: nonrepresentation requires q != 0; q = 0 gives both zero distributions. AComega also covers the volume/comparison and null-singleton suppliers; no singular Maxwell adoption follows.

items.title: Dimensional check of every Maxwell and Lorentz term in SI units
items.statement:
This example is conditional on the units of [[def-em-si-conventions]], the
definitions of divergence and curl in
[[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]], the equations of
[[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] and the coupling of [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]];
all equalities below are equalities of units, using
$1\ \mathrm{C}=1\ \mathrm{A\,s}$, $1\ \mathrm{V}=1\ \mathrm{J\,C^{-1}}$,
$1\ \mathrm{J}=1\ \mathrm{N\,m}$,
$1\ \mathrm{W}=1\ \mathrm{V\,A}=1\ \mathrm{J\,s^{-1}}$,
$1\ \mathrm{F}=1\ \mathrm{C\,V^{-1}}$ and
$1\ \mathrm{T}=1\ \mathrm{N\,A^{-1}\,m^{-1}}$.

(a) $\operatorname{div}E$ has unit $\mathrm{V\,m^{-2}}$ and
$\rho/\varepsilon_0$ has unit
$\mathrm{C\,m^{-3}/(F\,m^{-1})}=\mathrm{C\,V\,m^{-2}\,C^{-1}}
=\mathrm{V\,m^{-2}}$, so the two sides of
$\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0$ agree.

(b) $\operatorname{curl}B$ has unit $\mathrm{T\,m^{-1}}$; $\mu_0J$ has unit
$\mathrm{N\,A^{-2}\cdot A\,m^{-2}}=\mathrm{N\,A^{-1}\,m^{-2}}
=\mathrm{T\,m^{-1}}$; $c^{-2}\partial_tE$ has unit
$\mathrm{m^{-2}\,s^{2}\cdot V\,m^{-1}\,s^{-1}}=\mathrm{V\,s\,m^{-3}}
=\mathrm{N\,A^{-1}\,m^{-2}}=\mathrm{T\,m^{-1}}$, so both source terms of
$\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$ have the unit of
$\operatorname{curl}B$.

(c) $\operatorname{curl}E$ has unit
$\mathrm{V\,m^{-2}}=\mathrm{T\,s^{-1}}$ and $\partial_tB$ has unit
$\mathrm{T\,s^{-1}}$, so $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$ is homogeneous;
$\operatorname{div}B=0$ is a homogeneous equation.

(d) In the coupling of [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]], the adopted right-hand
side $q\,\Phi(U)$ has unit
$\mathrm{C\cdot T\cdot m\,s^{-1}}=\mathrm{C\,N\,A^{-1}\,s^{-1}}=\mathrm{N}$
(using $1\ \mathrm{T}=1\ \mathrm{N\,A^{-1}\,m^{-1}}$ and
$1\ \mathrm{C}=1\ \mathrm{A\,s}$) and the left-hand side $m\,dU/d\tau$ has unit
$\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-2}}=\mathrm{N}$, so the two sides of
$m\,dU/d\tau=q\,\Phi(U)$ agree; in the coordinate expression
$q(E+r'\times B)$ on the right of the postulate's displayed nonrelativistic
acceleration equation (that whole equation is not adopted as exact), $qE$ has unit
$\mathrm{C\cdot V\,m^{-1}}=\mathrm{J\,m^{-1}}=\mathrm{N}$ and
$q\,(r'\times B)$ has unit
$\mathrm{C\,m\,s^{-1}\,T}=\mathrm{C\,N\,A^{-1}\,s^{-1}}=\mathrm{N}$, so its
two terms add with the unit of a force; and $\rho E+J\times B$ has unit
$\mathrm{C\,m^{-3}\,V\,m^{-1}}=\mathrm{N\,m^{-3}}$, the unit of a force
density, while $J\cdot E$ has unit
$\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}\cdot V\,m^{-1}}=\mathrm{W\,m^{-3}}$, the unit of a power
density.

(e) The energy density $\tfrac12(\varepsilon_0E^2+B^2/\mu_0)$ has unit
$\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$ and the flux $E\times B/\mu_0$ has unit
$\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$, consistent with
$\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}\cdot m\,s^{-1}}=\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$.

(f) The check is exact arithmetic of the adopted units; it is not a
measurement, it does not prove the equations, and no numerical value of
$\mu_0$ is used or asserted.
items.strategy: Direct substitution in the unit table of [[def-em-si-conventions]]: each displayed unit computation is a product and quotient of the base and derived units listed there, with the conversion identities $1\ \mathrm{C}=1\ \mathrm{A\,s}$, $1\ \mathrm{V}=1\ \mathrm{J\,C^{-1}}$, $1\ \mathrm{J}=1\ \mathrm{N\,m}$ and $1\ \mathrm{T}=1\ \mathrm{N\,A^{-1}\,m^{-1}}$ quoted from the same source. The only structural input is that divergence divides a field unit by a length and curl does the same while preserving the field unit ([[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]); time derivatives divide by a time. All computations are finite and exact, and no empirical premise or measurement is used.
